The AP Exam

Your AP score is built from two things you can see coming from a mile away: a program you make in class (theCreate performance task,30% of the score) and one big sitting exam in May (the end-of-course exam, 70%). No surprises, no curves to game — just preparation.

Mark both dates: Create PT due2027-04-30, 11:59 PM ET in the AP Digital Portfolio. End-of-course exam Friday, May 14, 2027, 8:00 AM (Session 1), in Bluebook on a school laptop. The exam lands on an A-day Friday — this class does not meet, but you take the exam that morning.

The end-of-course exam (Friday, May 14, 2027)

A fully digital exam taken in the Bluebook app on a school laptop. Two sections, one sitting:

SectionWhatTimeWeight
Section I70 multiple-choice questions, 4 answer choices each: 57 single-select, 5 single-select with a reading passage about a computing innovation, and 8 multi-select (choose 2)120 min70% of score
Section II2 written-response questions aboutyour own Create program, answered with your Personalized Project Reference (PPR) in hand — four prompts: WR1, WR2(a), WR2(b), WR2(c)60 min(part of the Create PT's 30%)

The written-response section is why the Create PT matters so much: you cannot pass it without knowing your own program cold. We practice writing about your code every clinic from May 3 to May 13. See Written Responses.

The big ideas and their MC weights

Big ideaExam weightWhere we taught it
1. Creative Development10-13%All year: every jam, the boss spec, the Create PT
2. Data17-22%Unit 9: binary, hex, compression, datasets, bias
3. Algorithms and Programming30-35%Units 1-8: every script you wrote; card jam: lists
4. Computer Systems and Networks11-15%Unit 9: systems, the Internet, encryption
5. Impact of Computing21-26%Unit 9 + every jam retro and the licenses lesson

Notice what is missing: Java. The AP CSP exam is language-agnostic — its pseudocode looks a little like Python. All year we translate between C# and the exam's pseudocode in class; theExam Reference Sheet page has the full translation guide.

How to prepare (in order)

  1. Ship the Create PT early. Program by Apr 23, video + PPR by Apr 27, submitted Apr 29. It is 30% and it is fully in your control.
  2. Learn your own program cold. The written responses ask about YOUR list, YOUR procedure, YOUR algorithm. You wrote them — be able to explain them line by line.
  3. Grind the clinics. May 3-13 is four sessions of real practice sets under real timing. Treat them like the exam.
  4. Read carefully. Every MC question has one defensible answer and three trap answers built from real student misconceptions. The traps are predictable — see MC Strategy.
